content.value_statement: Teams need reliable visibility into services, errors, latency, and infrastructure health. This skill guides metrics, traces, logs, dashboards, alerts, SLOs, and monitoring infrastructure.
actual_capabilities: Design Prometheus scrape configurations and alert rules.
Create Grafana dashboard plans for service health metrics.
Plan OpenTelemetry tracing setup with Jaeger integration.
Define structured logging and log aggregation patterns.
Draft SLOs, error budgets, and incident response runbooks.
limitations: Does not deploy infrastructure or run commands by itself.
Requires real service names, metric names, and deployment details.
Generated examples need review before production use.
Does not replace incident management or on-call policy design.

use_cases.title: Launch Monitoring For A New Service
use_cases.description: Create an initial monitoring plan with metrics, traces, logs, dashboards, and alerts before production release.

use_cases.title: Improve Incident Visibility
use_cases.description: Identify missing telemetry and add dashboards, alerts, and runbooks that reduce diagnosis time.

use_cases.title: Standardize Observability Practices
use_cases.description: Define reusable patterns for Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, logging, SLOs, and infrastructure modules.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Basic Monitoring Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a monitoring plan for my application. Include key metrics, logs, traces, alerts, and one dashboard layout.

prompt_templates.title: Design Service Dashboards
prompt_templates.prompt: Design Grafana dashboards for a service with request rate, error rate, latency, saturation, and dependency health views.

prompt_templates.title: Add Tracing And Logging
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan OpenTelemetry tracing and structured logging for my service. Include propagation, resource attributes, sampling, and log correlation.

prompt_templates.title: Build A Production Observability Stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production observability stack for Kubernetes. Include Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager, log aggregation, SLOs, and runbooks.

output_examples.input: Plan observability for a Node.js API running on Kubernetes.
output: Assessment: the service needs request, latency, error, and saturation metrics.
Architecture: Prometheus scrapes application and node exporters, Grafana displays service dashboards, and OpenTelemetry exports traces.
Alerts: high error rate, slow response time, pod restarts, and memory pressure trigger runbooks.

output_examples.input: Improve alerts for a payment service with frequent false positives.
output: Alert review: separate customer impact alerts from noisy infrastructure warnings.
SLO plan: track successful payment authorization rate over rolling windows.
Runbook guidance: include likely causes, dashboards to inspect, and escalation owners.

output_examples.input: Create an observability standard for several backend teams.
output: Standard metrics: request count, duration, errors, queue depth, dependency latency, and resource usage.
Required labels: service, environment, version, region, and owner.
Governance: review dashboards and alerts during service readiness checks.

best_practices: Start with user-impacting signals before adding infrastructure detail.
Use consistent labels for service, environment, version, and owner.
Pair every actionable alert with a dashboard link and runbook.
anti_patterns: Creating alerts for every metric without clear action.
Using high-cardinality labels for request identifiers or user data.
Copying example thresholds into production without measuring baselines.

faq.question: What monitoring tools does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, Jaeger, Fluentd, Alertmanager, SLOs, and Terraform-based monitoring patterns.

faq.question: Can it generate production-ready dashboards?
faq.answer: It can draft dashboard structures and queries, but teams should validate metric names, labels, and thresholds.

faq.question: Does it execute setup commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides plans, examples, and configuration guidance for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Can it help with alert fatigue?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review alert intent, group alerts by impact, suggest thresholds, and add runbook guidance.

faq.question: Does it require Kubernetes?
faq.answer: No. Several examples use Kubernetes, but the patterns also apply to services on other platforms.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Store webhooks, API keys, and service keys in approved secret managers or deployment secrets.
